cards.text: Solomon has rested with his fathers, and his son Rehoboam is next in line for the throne (1 Kings 11:43). Now Rehoboam goes to Shechem, because all Israel has gone there to make him king. Big day, friend, and I bet the whole nation is waiting to see what the new guy is made of.
Meanwhile, Jeroboam son of Nebat, the servant who rebelled against Solomon, is still in Egypt where he fled from the king (1 Kings 11:26). Friend, that's not a trip, that's a forwarding address.

cards.question: The people send for Jeroboam, and he comes with the whole assembly of Israel to speak to Rehoboam.

cards.text: No small talk, no "congrats on the new job." They tell Rehoboam straight up, "Your father put a heavy yoke on us."

cards.question: The people say Solomon put a heavy yoke on them. What do they ask the new king Rehoboam to do?
If Rehoboam lightens their yoke, the people say they will serve him.

cards.text: Rehoboam doesn't answer on the spot: "Go away for three days and then return to me." So the people head out.
While the people are gone, King Rehoboam asks the elders who served his father Solomon how he should respond. Smart move, friend: these guys have seen it ALL.

cards.question: The elders who served Solomon answer King Rehoboam. What do they advise him to do?

answers.text: Serve the people and speak kindly
Wait until the people calm down

cards.question: The elders tell Rehoboam that if he serves the people and speaks kind words to them, the people will be his ___ forever.
King Rehoboam takes the advice of the elders who served his father.

cards.text: Rehoboam rejects the elders and asks the young men who grew up with him and served him. That's like ignoring the mechanic and asking your buddy who watched ONE video.

cards.question: The young men who grew up with Rehoboam give him their advice. What kind of answer do they want him to give the people?

answers.text: One that sounds tougher than his father
One that sounds gentler than his father
One that asks the people for more time

cards.text: Their opening line for him: "My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist!" Friend, that's not an answer, that's a FLEX.

cards.question: What do the young men tell Rehoboam to say he'll do with the heavy yoke his father put on the people?

cards.text: And they top it off: "Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions." Whips to SCORPIONS?! Who signed off on this?
Three days later, just like the king said, Jeroboam and all the people come back to Rehoboam. Everybody is waiting on one answer.

cards.question: Jeroboam and the people are back for their answer. How does King Rehoboam speak to them?

answers.text: Harshly like the young men advised

cards.text: He gives them the young men's advice: a heavier yoke, and scorpions instead of whips. Of all the lines he could have let go, friend, he held on to the SCORPIONS.
So the king doesn't listen to the people. But the writer lets us in on something bigger going on behind it all.

cards.question: This turn of events was from the LORD, to fulfill what He had spoken to Jeroboam through Ahijah the Shilonite, a prophet (1 Kings 11:29).
All Israel sees that King Rehoboam has refused to listen to them. How do they answer him?

answers.text: They want no part in David's house
They agree to serve him anyway
They ask for three more days

cards.text: "To your tents, O Israel!" they say, and the Israelites go home. That's the whole room walking out of the meeting.

cards.question: After the Israelites go home, Rehoboam doesn't reign over any Israelites at all.

cards.text: Then King Rehoboam sends out Adoram, the man in charge of the forced labor. Of everybody he could send, he picks the forced labor guy.

cards.question: King Rehoboam sends Adoram, who is in charge of the forced labor, out to all Israel. What do they do to him?

answers.text: They agree to work for him

cards.text: King Rehoboam mounts his chariot in haste and escapes to Jerusalem. No goodbye speech, no "thanks for coming," just GONE.
And the writer says it plainly: to this day Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David.

cards.question: When all Israel hears that Jeroboam has returned, they call him to the assembly and make him ___ over all Israel.
Once Jeroboam is made king, only the tribe of Judah still follows the house of David.
Back in Jerusalem, Rehoboam gathers Judah and Benjamin, 180,000 chosen warriors, to fight against the house of ___.

cards.text: But the word of God comes to Shemaiah, a man of God, with a message for Rehoboam king of Judah and all the people with him. I bet Shemaiah's knees were knocking with 180,000 warriors in front of him.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell Rehoboam and his warriors through Shemaiah, the man of God?

answers.text: Don't fight your brothers and go home
Go up and win the kingdom back
Wait three days and then attack

cards.question: The LORD tells the warriors to return home, because this is His doing.
180,000 warriors are ready to fight, and the LORD says go home. What do they do?

cards.text: Don't hang up your apron yet, friend. This kingdom's story is NOT over.
